headline: Local officials face death threats and gunfire over AI data center projects; 500+ towns restrict builds
summary: Across the US, local officials are receiving death threats and experiencing violence related to proposed AI data center projects, leading to over 500 towns restricting new builds.
details: Officials in Marshall, Michigan, received a credible death threat after passing a one-year moratorium on new data center builds. This incident is part of a growing trend of local government leaders facing intimidation.

Similar situations have unfolded in Salix, Iowa, and Box Elder County, Utah, where officials reported threats after considering or approving data center projects. NBC News confirmed that city leaders nationwide are now receiving death threats.

Previous incidents include 13 rounds fired into an Indianapolis councilman's home after he supported rezoning for a project. In Michigan, a treasurer resigned citing threats over a 1.4GW Oracle and OpenAI campus, which triggered moratoriums in 19 municipalities.

The town of Salix, Iowa, postponed a moratorium vote due to online posts calling for "various death and terroristic type things" against its government. The Woodbury County Sheriff's Office is investigating these threats.

In Box Elder County, Utah, commissioners received threats after voting for the Stratos project area, with an audience chanting "shame." Emporia, Kansas, moved commission meetings online and dropped public comment due to threats against its leaders.

A Soufan Center IntelBrief, based on X and Reddit data, found hundreds of posts with threat language between July 2025 and July 2026, with a volume surge beginning in April. Most violent threats target infrastructure, but some name council members and planning commissions.

These online threats often use memes, emojis, and misspellings to evade moderation, and new incidents now draw significant secondary amplification. As a result, over 500 local restrictions on data centers are now in place nationwide, with many towns canceling or restricting public meetings.
